```{python}
#| label: setup
#| warning: false
#| message: false
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from gapminder import gapminder
```
 
This post uses the gapminder dataset to look at life expectancy across 142
different countries from 1952 to 2007.
 
Data: Based on free material from [GAPMINDER.ORG](https://www.gapminder.org/data/),
CC-BY licence, from the gapminder Python package.
 
## Life Expectancy by continent
 
I took the averaged life expectancy across the countries in each continent for
every survey year (1952–2007) to compare how life expectancy has changed in
each continent.
 
```{python}
continent_trend = (
    gapminder
    .groupby(["continent", "year"], as_index=False)
    .agg(mean_life=("lifeExp", "mean"))
)
continent_trend.head()
```

 
```{python}
#| label: fig-continent-trend
#| fig-cap: "Mean life expectancy by continent, 1952–2007."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
for continent, group in continent_trend.groupby("continent"):
    ax.plot(group["year"], group["mean_life"], marker="o", linewidth=2,
            label=continent)
ax.set_ylabel("Mean life expectancy (years)")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
plt.show()
```
 

As @fig-continent-trend shows, life expectancy has consistently been highest
in Oceania (which in this dataset is only Australia and New Zealand) and lowest
in Africa. Every continent's life expectancy rose between 1952 and 2007, and
all except Africa increased in every survey year. Africa's average stalled
from the late 1980s and dipped slightly between 1992 and 2002, before rising
again by 2007.
 
## Which country gained the most?
 
Next I calculated the change in life expectancy for each country between
1952 and 2007.
 
```{python}
life_change = (
    gapminder[gapminder["year"].isin([1952, 2007])]
    .pivot_table(index=["country", "continent"], columns="year",
                 values="lifeExp")
    .reset_index()
)
life_change.columns = ["country", "continent", "1952", "2007"]
life_change["change"] = life_change["2007"] - life_change["1952"]
life_change = life_change.sort_values("change", ascending=False,
                                      ignore_index=True)
 
n_declined = int((life_change["change"] < 0).sum())
top_country = life_change["country"].iloc[0]
top_change = f"{life_change['change'].iloc[0]:.1f}"
bottom_country = life_change["country"].iloc[-1]
bottom_change = f"{life_change['change'].iloc[-1]:.1f}"
```
 

The five biggest gains and the five biggest losses:
 
```{python}
#| label: life-change-extremes
pd.concat([life_change.head(5), life_change.tail(5)]).round(1)
```
 
`{python} top_country` gained the most, `{python} top_change` years. At the
other end, `{python} n_declined` countries had a *lower* life expectancy in
2007 than in 1952. The largest drop was in `{python} bottom_country`
(`{python} bottom_change` years).
